correctness.rationale: Independent uniform endpoint angles on radii 1 and R make the outer chord line offset H arcsine on [-R,R], independent of its normal; a crossing occurs precisely when H falls between the two inner endpoint projections. Their arcsine CDF F gives G(h)=2F(h)(1-F(h)), yielding p(R)=pi^-1 int_{-1}^1 G(x)/sqrt(R^2-x^2) dx for R>=1. Positive binomial expansion proves c_n>0 and strict complete monotonicity; the sum at R=1 equals 1/3 and the n=0 term 8/pi^3 yields sharp global bounds. Endpoint G(1-s)~(2sqrt(2)/pi)s^1/2 gives c_n~1/(pi^2n^2), whose dilogarithmic partial-sum singularity yields (2/pi^2)epsilon log(1/epsilon). Independently integrated the first three c_n and five radii, verifying coefficients and bounds; the proof, not simulations, controls all R and the infinite cusp.
residual_risks: Only endpoint-uniform independent straight finite chords, concentric radii R>=1; p(1) has infinite negative right derivative, not differentiable at the collision.

value.rationale: The equal-radius limit is a singular collision of endpoint-supported chord laws: the first derivative diverges while the function stays continuous. The exact positive-series decomposition simultaneously yields strong shape information, strictly alternating derivatives and globally sharp scale-corrected bounds. These are motivated natural invariants of two nested circles and not a recomputation of 1/3 alone.
residual_risks: Significance limited to this endpoint-uniform chord model; not a universal random-line convention.
